claim_text: Detox drinks and herbal cleanses flush out toxins and cleanse the liver.
raw_quotes: Clean your liver in just one night
mechanism: Medical research shows the liver cleans itself. It does not need herbal or detox drinks advertised as 'liver cleansers', whether made at home or bought from online stores.
risk_rationale: Using too much of these drinks can cause liver poisoning.
true_part: The liver already works as a body cleaner and gets rid of unwanted substances.
overstated_part: That the liver needs an external cleaner and that detox drinks clean the liver.

evidence.title: Hepatotoxicity due to dietary supplements: state-of-the-art, gaps and perspectives
evidence.note: Reviews liver damage caused by dietary supplements (safety).

evidence.title: Detoxification pathways in the liver
evidence.note: Describes the liver's own built-in detoxification pathways (mechanism).

recommended_action: Maintain a healthy lifestyle: eat balanced food, drink enough water, exercise, and keep a healthy weight.

claim_text: Drinking garlic water daily eliminates bacteria and viruses in the body.
raw_quotes: This is the garlic water that will do wonder for your body
drink one cup of garlic water daily and thank me later

clickbait_phrases: will do wonder for your body

mechanism: Raw garlic and garlic water contain a compound called allicin, which has antibacterial properties proven only in lab tests (in test tubes). However, it cannot kill bacteria inside the human body with the same efficiency.
risk_rationale: It causes irritation and erosion of the stomach wall, as well as disruption of good gut bacteria, if used daily. It also poses a risk for people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
true_part: Garlic contains organosulfur compounds like allicin that show antibacterial and antiviral properties in laboratory settings.
overstated_part: Claiming garlic water eradicates viral or bacterial infections inside the human body.

evidence.title: Nutraceutical use of garlic sulfur-containing compounds
evidence.note: Reviews garlic's sulfur compounds and their possible health uses (mechanism).

evidence.title: Effects of garlic preparations on the gastrointestinal mucosa
evidence.note: Raw garlic can damage the stomach lining (safety).

recommended_action: Eat cooked garlic by adding it to your food; this reduces its strong effect on the stomach. Eat foods that support good bacteria, like yogurt and buttermilk. If you have irritable bowel syndrome, ask a doctor first.

claim_text: Drinking alkaline water destroys cancer cells.
raw_quotes: No disease even cancer can't survive in an alkaline body

absolute_promises: No disease even cancer can't survive

mechanism: Blood pH is stable and stays between 7.35 and 7.45. Alkaline water cannot change blood pH. In fact, cancer cells create an acidic environment around themselves because they grow fast. An acidic environment does not cause cancer.
risk_rationale: Severe metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia that can threaten the heart, failure to absorb oral cancer drugs, and delaying real treatment due to false hope.
true_part: Alkaline water neutralizes stomach acid temporarily on contact.
overstated_part: Claiming it permanently neutralizes blood acidity or treats cancer.

evidence.title: Associations between per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and county-level cancer incidence between 2016 and 2021 and incident cancer burden attributable to PFAS in drinking water in the United States
Systematic review of the association between dietary acid load, alkaline water and cancer
evidence.note: Systematic review: no evidence that alkaline water or diet acid load treats or prevents cancer.

recommended_action: See a doctor if you have any symptoms of cancer and follow your doctor's instructions.
needs_review: one-line note missing for some PMIDs

claim_text: Apple cider vinegar breaks down kidney stones.
raw_quotes: your doctor will never tell you about this ingredient

clickbait_phrases: your doctor will never tell you about this ingredient

mechanism: Adding apple cider vinegar to the diet may help prevent kidney stones, but it fails to break down large or existing stones.
risk_rationale: Taking too much concentrated apple cider vinegar daily on an empty stomach can damage tooth enamel, make gums sensitive, and slow stomach emptying, which is risky for people with diabetes or gastroparesis.
true_part: Apple cider vinegar contains acetic and citric acid.
overstated_part: Claiming that drinking vinegar directly dissolves existing calcium kidney stones.

evidence.title: Apple cider vinegar for prevention of urinary lithiasis (APUL): a randomized crossover trial
evidence.note: Clinical trial of apple cider vinegar for preventing stones (prevention, not dissolving).

recommended_action: Consult your doctor and follow the medical treatment plan if you have kidney stones. Drink plenty of water.

claim_text: Bitter apricot kernels (vitamin B17) destroy cancer cells instantly.
raw_quotes: Fighting cancer or any other sickness? Add this to your medicine cabinet

clickbait_phrases: Add this to your medicine cabinet

mechanism: Apricot kernels are promoted as 'vitamin B17', which is not a vitamin. They contain amygdalin, which turns into toxic cyanide inside the body. Laetrile is a lab-made version that works the same way.
risk_rationale: Cyanide poisoning, which can lead to death and makes cancer patients severely ill.
true_part: Bitter apricot seeds contain high concentrations of amygdalin.
overstated_part: Claiming vitamin B17 cures or destroys cancer cells and that you will not need any medical treatment.

evidence.title: Laetrile treatment for cancer
evidence.note: Cochrane review: no reliable evidence laetrile/amygdalin helps cancer; risk of cyanide poisoning.

evidence.title: A clinical trial of amygdalin (Laetrile) in the treatment of human cancer
evidence.note: Clinical trial: amygdalin gave no substantial benefit to cancer patients.

recommended_action: Consult your doctor. Do not take advertised cancer treatments or follow random medical advice, especially with a chronic or serious illness.

claim_text: Drinking dry chia seeds with warm water and lemon blocks fat absorption and causes rapid weight loss.
raw_quotes: Do you even imagine what miracle chia seeds with lemon can do

clickbait_phrases: Do you even imagine what miracle chia seeds with lemon can do

mechanism: Chia seeds alone do not burn fat. They are high in fiber, which makes you feel full longer, but they do not cause weight loss without a calorie deficit. Lemon does not burn fat either.
risk_rationale: Swallowing dry chia seeds lets them swell in the food pipe and stomach, which can cause breathing difficulty and esophageal blockage.
true_part: Chia seeds contain a high percentage of fiber, which makes you feel full.
overstated_part: Claiming chia gel creates a barrier that blocks fat absorption or triggers rapid weight loss.

evidence.title: Chia seed does not promote weight loss or alter disease risk factors in overweight adults
evidence.note: Randomized trial: chia seeds did not cause weight loss in overweight adults.

recommended_action: To lose weight you need a calorie deficit with a diet plan and exercise; consult a nutritionist who knows your medical history.

claim_text: Activated charcoal whitens teeth at home.
raw_quotes: Whiten your teeth in 2 minutes at home
mechanism: Using activated charcoal to whiten teeth has no real benefit. It does not change tooth color chemically; it acts like an abrasive.
risk_rationale: It erodes enamel and exposes the yellower, more sensitive layer underneath. Ordinary (non-activated) charcoal adds risk of toxicity and irritation.
true_part: Activated charcoal can physically scrub away superficial surface stains (from coffee, tea, or food) through mild mechanical abrasion.
overstated_part: Claims that charcoal bleaches teeth in depth like a real whitening treatment and is safe for daily use without wearing down enamel or causing tooth pain.

evidence.title: Charcoal and charcoal-based dentifrices: A literature review
Effectiveness and abrasiveness of activated charcoal as a whitening agent: A systematic review of in vitro studies

recommended_action: Consult your dentist about professional whitening, and avoid DIY remedies such as charcoal or baking soda.

claim_text: Antibiotics treat the flu and common colds.
raw_quotes: I found an antibiotic that works very well for cold

clickbait_phrases: I found an antibiotic that works very well

mechanism: Antibiotics target and kill bacteria only. They have no effect on viruses, which cause the flu and common colds.
risk_rationale: Improper use destroys both helpful and harmful bacteria and drives antibiotic resistance, so future bacterial infections become harder to treat.
true_part: Antibiotics are powerful medications designed specifically to treat bacterial infections.
overstated_part: Claiming antibiotics cure colds or other viral infections.

evidence.title: Antibiotics for the common cold and acute purulent rhinitis
evidence.note: Cochrane review: antibiotics do not help the common cold and cause side effects.

evidence.title: Antibiotics for the common cold

recommended_action: If you have a cold, see a doctor to manage symptoms, and avoid antibiotics since they do not work on viruses.
needs_review: one-line note missing for some PMIDs

claim_text: Castor oil eye drops treat cataracts and improve vision.
raw_quotes: How Castor oil can improve your vision

clickbait_phrases: How Castor oil can improve your vision

mechanism: Castor oil cannot penetrate the eye or treat the lens. Cataracts are caused by protein clumping inside the inner lens, so oil cannot reach or dissolve it. The only proven treatment is surgery.
risk_rationale: Cell toxicity, severe irritation and inflammation, and permanent vision loss due to delayed treatment.
true_part: Sterile castor oil formulations are used in specialized lipid-based eye drops to lubricate the eye surface and reduce dry-eye symptoms.
overstated_part: Claims that castor oil dissolves cataracts or reverses vision loss.

evidence.title: Benefits and side effects of different vegetable oil vectors on apoptosis, oxidative stress, and P2X7 cell death receptor activation
evidence.note: Lab study of vegetable oils on eye cells, including toxic effects (safety); not a cataract trial.

recommended_action: If you have cataracts, see an eye doctor about treatment such as surgery. Do not put oils or other substances in your eyes unless prescribed.

claim_text: Applying toothpaste to burns heals them.
mechanism: Toothpaste does not treat or soothe burns. It only gives a false feeling of relief because menthol feels cool, but it causes damage later.
risk_rationale: It worsens the burn and can cause infection; it also sticks to the burn and is painful to remove in the ER.
true_part: Menthol in toothpaste gives a brief, temporary cooling feeling on the skin surface.
overstated_part: Claiming toothpaste heals burns or is a first-aid measure for burns.

evidence.title: Perception, Awareness, and Practices Related to Burn First Aid Among the General Population in Qassim Region, Saudi Arabia
Review of Traditional First Aid for Burn Injuries in the 21st Century

recommended_action: For a minor burn, cool it under running water, apply a burn ointment, and do not pop blisters. For a deep burn, go to the hospital.

claim_text: Uncalibrated at-home UV tanning lamps are a safe way to get a quick tan.
raw_quotes: Glow up in minutes with this tanning lamp
mechanism: Tanning devices that use UVA rays penetrate deep into the skin and damage the DNA of skin cells; their damage is higher than sun exposure. The tan is melanin produced to protect cells from radiation.
risk_rationale: Skin cancer, especially with repeated use, and faster skin aging from collagen damage.
true_part: Artificial UV tanning lamps emit high-intensity ultraviolet radiation (UVA/UVB) that stimulates skin cells to produce melanin.
overstated_part: Claiming they offer a safe, fast tan without any risks.

evidence.title: Use of tanning devices and risk of basal cell and squamous cell skin cancers
Ultraviolet radiation and skin cancer

recommended_action: Use sunless tanning creams from a safe brand (patch-test first), and wear sunscreen outdoors.

claim_text: Applying crushed raw garlic to the scalp cures hair loss.
raw_quotes: Rub garlic on your scalp and you will thank me later
mechanism: Raw garlic on the scalp does not reach the hair roots. Its strong sulfur compounds act like burning chemicals, irritating the skin instead of helping hair grow.
risk_rationale: Chemical burns and permanent scarring hair loss (scarring alopecia), plus tissue damage.
true_part: Lab-formulated garlic gels, used under expert supervision, contain sulfur compounds that can increase scalp blood flow and soothe hair-follicle inflammation.
overstated_part: Claiming raw crushed garlic reverses hair loss or baldness.

evidence.title: Garlic burn injuries- a systematic review of reported cases
evidence.note: Systematic review of cases where raw garlic on skin caused burns (safety).

recommended_action: See a doctor to find the cause of your hair loss and get the right treatment.

claim_text: Using ice consistently gives glowing skin.
true_part: Ice causes local vasoconstriction and reduces swelling, causing a temporary rush of blood flow and a minor cooling flush when removed.
overstated_part: Claims that using ice daily improves skin texture, shrinks pores, and replaces skincare or seeing a doctor.

evidence.title: Effect of cold face stimulation on cerebral blood flow in humans
